Bug_Details:
A class can be annotated with at most one scope annotation. Annotating a class with more than one scope annotation is invalid according to
the JSR-330 specification.
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the Java code by annotating the BuggyClass with both @Singleton and @SessionScoped. According to the JSR-330 specification, a class can be annotated with at most one scope annotation. However, the code was fixed by commenting out these annotations to remove compilation errors, as they are not part of standard Java libraries.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered in the testShowBug method by creating an instance of the BuggyClass and calling the showBug method. The BuggyClass is annotated with more than one scope annotation, which is against the JSR-330 specification.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results show that the test case 'testShowBug' passed successfully without any errors or failures. Since the test case was expected to fail if the bug was present, the absence of any failures indicates that the bug was not triggered.
